texts.preamble: In Re vs A-1) Manoj Kumar on 28 April, 2016 In The Court Of Sh. Ashu Garg, Addl. Chief Metropolitan Magistrate - Ii (New Delhi), Patiala House Courts, New Delhi Cc No. 51 / 15 Unique Case Id No. 02403R0023112011 Date of Institution: 09.03.2011 Date of reserving judgement: 29.03.2016 Date of pronouncement: 28.04.2016 In re: Delhi Administration / Food Inspector Department of Pfa, Govt. of Nct of Delhi A-20, Lawrence Road Industrial Area, Delhi-110035 ... Complainant versus A-1) Manoj Kumar S/o. Sh. Desh Raj R/o. T - 39, First Floor, Village Tehkhand, Okhla, Phase - I, New Delhi-110 020 A-2) M/s. Manoj Sweets. R/o. T-39, First Floor, Village Tehkhand, Okhla, Phase - I, New Delhi-110 020 ... Accused Cc No. 51/11 Page 1 of 9 Judgment:
texts.facts: 1. The present is a complaint filed under section 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (PFA Act), alleging that the accused persons has violated the provisions of the PFA Act and Rules. The accused is stated to be the vendor-cum- proprietor of M/s. Manoj Sweets, from where the food article, that is, 'boondi ke laddoo' was lifted for sampling. 2. As per the complaint, on 03.08.2010, the food officials consisting of Food Inspector (FI) P. M. Kothekar and Field Assistant (FA) S. Maissey under the supervision of Local Health Authority (LHA)/SDM Sh. V. P. Singh reached along with their staff at the premises of M/s. Manoj Sweets at In Re vs A-1) Manoj Kumar on 28 April, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191839841/ 1 shop No. T-39, Village Tehkhand, Okhla, New Delhi-110020, where the accused was found conducting the business of various food articles, which were lying stored for sale for human consumption. The FI disclosed his identity and expressed his intention to purchase a sample of boondi ke laddoo from the vendor, lying there in open tray bearing no label declaration, to which he agreed. The sample was then lifted as per procedure prescribed under the PFA Act and Rules. Each sample was separately packed, fastened, marked and sealed and necessary documents were prepared at the spot, including the Notice as per Form-VI, panchnama, etc. The price of sample was paid to the vendor. Thereafter, one counterpart of the sample was sent to the Public Analyst (PA) in intact condition and the other two counterparts were deposited with SDM/LHA. Vide report dated 27.08.2010, the PA found the sample to be "misbranded" on the ground that the presence of synthetic colour was not declared as one of the ingredients. Upon receipt of report, the SDM/LHA ordered investigation which was carried out by FI. After completion of investigation, sanction under section 20 of the PFA Act was obtained from the Director PFA. The complaint was then filed in the court on 09.03.2011 alleging violation of section 2(ia)(a) and (m) PFA Act and also Section 2 (ix) (d) and (e) of PFA Act, as punishable section 7/16(1A) of PFA Act. 3. As the complaint was filed in writing by a public servant, recording of pre-summoning evidence was dispensed with and the accused was summoned vide order dated 09.03.2011. 4. Notice of accusation under section 251 Cr.P.C was framed against the accused on 29.08.2012 for commission of the offence punishable under section 7/16(1)(a) PFA Act, being violation of section 2 (ix) (d) and (e) of PFA Act, to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. It is pertinent to note that no notice was framed for violation of Section 2 (ia) (a) and (m) of PFA Act despite the complaint mentioning them, probably in view of the PA report. 5. At the trial, prosecution examined three witnesses in support of its case. PW-1 FI, PW-2 SDM / LHA and PW-3 FA were part of the team that had visited the spot for sample proceedings. All these witnesses deposed about the proceedings conducted by them on 03.08.2010 and narrated the steps undertaken by them during the sample proceedings, including disclosing their identity, expressing intention to purchase sample for analysis, lifting the sample of 1500 grams of boondi ke laddoo, dividing it in three parts, sealing, marking the samples, and obtaining signatures of vendor and witnesses. They also proved the necessary documents including the vendor's receipt Ex.PW-1/A, Notice in Form VI Ex. PW-1/B, Panchnama Ex. PW-1/C, Report under Rule 9 (e) Ex. PW-1/D. Receipt of PA Ex. PW-1/F and LHA receipt Ex. PW-1/G. PA report Ex. PW-1/H was received and after obtaining consent of Director, PFA Ex.PW1/J, complaint Ex.PW1/K was filed. These witnesses were duly cross-examined by Ld. Defence Counsel wherein they denied that the sampling method was not proper or that the accused had been falsely implicated. 6. Statement of the accused under section 313 CrPC was recorded on 17.09.2014 wherein he denied the allegations and pleaded innocence. Though he admitted the proceedings dated 03.08.2010, yet he claimed that the food article was not made by him and he had bought the same from some other person. He denied the Public Analyst report. He chose not to lead evidence in defence. In Re vs A-1) Manoj Kumar on 28 April, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191839841/ 2 7. It is in these circumstances, Ld. SPP for the complainant has argued that the complainant has been able to establish its case against the accused beyond reasonable doubt, on the ground that the accused has not been able to rebut the findings of PA report dated 27.08.2010.
texts.arguments: It is submitted that all the witnesses have supported its case and no major contradiction can be seen in their testimony. 8. On the other hand, Ld. Defence Counsel has submitted that the present is not a case of misbranding as there is nothing to show that the article was coloured or polished to conceal the fact that it was damaged or it was made to appear of a greater value or that no any false claim had been made on its label.
texts.respondent_arguments: It is submitted that all the witnesses have supported its case and no major contradiction can be seen in their testimony. 8. On the other hand, Ld.
